claims.statement: Tartaros was a primordial god of the underworld pit.
claims.statement_id: Tartaros ialah dewa purba yang mewujudkan jurang bawah tanah.
claims.quote: TARTAROS (Tartarus) was the primordial god (protogenos) of the stormy pit of Tartaros

claims.statement: He embodied the pit rather than a human-shaped deity.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipahami sebagai jurang itu sendiri, bukan sosok manusia.
claims.quote: He was the body of the pit itself rather than an athropomorphic deity.

claims.statement: Tartarus was the lowest point of the cosmos, separate from the underworld.
claims.statement_id: Tartarus berada di titik terbawah kosmos, terpisah dari dunia orang mati.
claims.quote: Tartarus was the lowest point of the universe, below the underworld but separate from it.

claims.statement: Tartarus was among the first beings of the Greek cosmos.
claims.statement_id: Tartarus termasuk makhluk pertama dalam kosmogoni Yunani.
claims.quote: as one of the first beings to come into existence in the universe

claims.statement: As an elemental deity, Tartaros rarely acts as a mythic character.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai dewa elemental, Tartarus jarang berperan sebagai tokoh dalam kisah.
claims.quote: The protogenos (primordial deity) Tartaros scarcely figures in myth and was a purely elemental deity

claims.statement: Tartarus and Gaia parented Typhon.
claims.statement_id: Tartarus dan Gaia memiliki anak bernama Typhon.
claims.quote: Tartarus and Gaia had a child, Typhon.

claims.statement: The pit was portrayed as a dark prison with iron gates.
claims.statement_id: Jurangnya juga digambarkan sebagai penjara gelap berpintu besi.
claims.quote: is a dark underground prison with iron gates

claims.statement: Zeus cast Cronus and the Titans there.
claims.statement_id: Zeus mengurung Cronus dan para Titan di sana.
claims.quote: whither Cronus and the Titans were thrust down by Zeus

claims.statement: Later authors made Tartarus a place of postmortem punishment.
claims.statement_id: Penulis belakangan menjadikannya tempat hukuman bagi orang jahat setelah mati.
claims.quote: Later writers make Tartarus the place of punishment of the wicked after death

claims.statement: Mythic descriptions give Tartarus bronze walls and Hekatonkheires guards.
claims.statement_id: Dalam gambaran mitis, Tartarus berdinding perunggu dan dijaga Hekatonkheires.
claims.quote: Tartaros was secured with a surrounding wall of bronze set with a pair of gates guarded by the hundred-handed Hekatonkheires.

claims.statement: Early accounts distinguish Hades from the pit of Tartarus.
claims.statement_id: Pada gambaran awal, Hades berbeda dari jurang Tartarus.
claims.quote: Haides, was originally quite distinct from the pit of Tartaros.

claims.statement: Hesiodic genealogy has Tartarus emerge without parents.
claims.statement_id: Dalam silsilah Hesiod, Tartarus muncul tanpa orang tua.
claims.quote: [1.1] NONE (one of the first to emerge at creation) (Hesiod Theogony 116)

claims.statement: Another genealogy makes Tartarus son of Æther and Ge.
claims.statement_id: Dalam silsilah lain, Tartarus adalah anak Æther dan Ge.
claims.quote: Tartarus is personified as the son of Æther and Ge

claims.statement: Later classical writers imagined Tartarus as a prison for the damned.
claims.statement_id: Tafsir klasik kemudian mengubah gambaran Tartarus menjadi penjara bagi yang terkutuk.
claims.quote: Later, classical writers re-imagined Tartaros as a hellish prison-house for the damned

claims.statement: Tartarus lies beneath the foundations of Earth.
claims.statement_id: Tartarus ditempatkan di bawah dasar bumi.
claims.quote: TARTAROS (Tartarus) was the primordial god (protogenos) of the stormy pit of Tartaros that lies beneath the foundations of the earth.

claims.statement: Themis is a Titan goddess of divine law and order.
claims.statement_id: Themis dewi Titan hukum dan tatanan ilahi.
claims.quote: THEMIS was the Titan goddess of divine law and order

claims.statement: Themis personifies divine law and justice in Greek mythology.
claims.statement_id: Themis mewujudkan hukum dan keadilan ilahi dalam mitologi Yunani.
claims.quote: Themis is the personification and goddess of divine law, will, and justice in Greek mythology.

claims.statement: Hesiod names Gaia and Uranus as Themis's parents.
claims.statement_id: Themis anak Gaia dan Uranus menurut Hesiod.
claims.quote: Themis is the daughter of Gaia (Earth) and Uranus (Heaven).

claims.statement: Themis was an early bride and counsellor of Zeus.
claims.statement_id: Themis pasangan awal dan penasihat Zeus.
claims.quote: Themis was an early bride of Zeus and his first counsellor.

claims.statement: Themis bore the Horae and Moirae with Zeus.
claims.statement_id: Themis melahirkan Horae dan Moirae dari Zeus.
claims.quote: She bore him six daughters, the three Horai (Horae, Seasons) and three Moirai (Moirae, Fates).

claims.statement: Themis held the Delphi oracle before Apollo.
claims.statement_id: Themis terkait orakel Delphi sebelum Apollo.
claims.quote: Themis held the place of Oracle at Delphi before passing on her prophetic powers to Apollo.

claims.statement: She summoned assemblies of gods and humans.
claims.statement_id: Ia memanggil sidang para dewa dan manusia.
claims.quote: her chief function being to summon the assemblies of both gods and men

claims.statement: Themis attends to rights of hospitality.
claims.statement_id: Themis mengawasi hak keramahtamahan.
claims.quote: takes special cognizance of the rights of hospitality

claims.statement: Art depicts Themis with a cornucopia and scales.
claims.statement_id: Seni menampilkan Themis dengan kornukopia dan timbangan.
claims.quote: with the cornucopiae (symbolizing the blessings resulting from order) and a pair of scales

claims.statement: The Greek word themis referred to customary divine law.
claims.statement_id: Kata Yunani themis berarti hukum ilahi berdasarkan adat.
claims.quote: In Greek, the word themis referred to divine law, those rules of conduct long established by custom.

claims.statement: Aeschylus gives the succession Gaia, Themis, Phoebe, Apollo.
claims.statement_id: Versi Aeschylus: Gaia, Themis, Phoebe, Apollo.
claims.quote: According to Aeschylus, Delphi was passed down in succession – Gaia passed it on to her daughter Themis who then passed it on to her sister, the Titaness Phoebe, who handed it over to Apollo.

claims.statement: Pausanias says Themis passed the oracle directly to Apollo.
claims.statement_id: Versi Pausanias: Themis menyerahkan orakel langsung kepada Apollo.
claims.quote: Themis passed it on to Apollo.

claims.statement: An Orphic hymn calls her prophetess of the gods.
claims.statement_id: Himne Orfik menyebutnya peramal para dewa.
claims.quote: In the Orphic Hymn to Themis, she is referred to as the "prophetess of the gods"

claims.statement: Themis had a shrine in Attica.
claims.statement_id: Themis memiliki tempat suci di Attika.
claims.quote: Themis had a shrine dedicated to her in Attica.

claims.statement: One account places Themis after Metis among Zeus's brides.
claims.statement_id: Satu silsilah menempatkannya setelah Metis.
claims.quote: Themis was one of the first brides of Zeus, second only to Metis

claims.statement: Pindar calls Themis Zeus's first bride.
claims.statement_id: Pindar menyebut Themis pasangan pertama Zeus.
claims.quote: there to be the primal bride of Zeus Soter (Saviour)

claims.statement: Cupid is a god of love and son of Venus.
claims.statement_id: Cupid ialah dewa cinta dan anak Venus dalam tradisi Romawi.
claims.quote: Cupid is the son of Venus and the god of Love

claims.statement: His Latin name is Amor and his Greek counterpart is Eros.
claims.statement_id: Nama Latin lainnya Amor; padanan Yunani ialah Eros.
claims.quote: in Latin he is called Amor, and in Greek, Eros

claims.statement: Cupid is usually depicted as a winged child.
claims.statement_id: Cupid biasa digambarkan sebagai anak bersayap.
claims.quote: He is usually shown as a winged child.

claims.statement: His attributes are bow, arrow and quiver.
claims.statement_id: Busur, panah, dan tabung panah adalah atributnya.
claims.quote: His attributes are a bow, arrow and quiver.

claims.statement: Those struck by Cupid's arrows fall in love.
claims.statement_id: Panah Cupid menyebabkan orang yang terkena jatuh cinta.
claims.quote: Those hit by his arrows become lovers.

claims.statement: Eros is depicted as Aphrodite’s companion.
claims.statement_id: Eros digambarkan sebagai pendamping Afrodit.
claims.quote: EROS was the mischievous god of love, a minion and constant companion of the goddess Aphrodite

claims.statement: In the Psyche story Venus calls her son Cupid.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Psyche, Venus memanggil putranya Cupid.
claims.quote: Venus summoned her son Cupid (Eros), the god of physical love and desire.

claims.statement: Venus ordered Cupid to punish Psyche through love.
claims.statement_id: Venus memerintahkannya menghukum Psyche dengan cinta yang tidak diinginkan.
claims.quote: commanded him to make Psyche fall in love with some hideous creature to punish her

claims.statement: Cupid accidentally wounded himself with his own arrow.
claims.statement_id: Cupid justru melukai dirinya dengan panahnya sendiri.
claims.quote: Cupid, who wounded himself with his own arrow in the confusion.

claims.statement: Cupid then fell in love with Psyche.
claims.statement_id: Cupid kemudian jatuh cinta kepada Psyche.
claims.quote: Thereafter, Cupid fell helplessly in love with Psyche.

claims.statement: Apuleius tells the Cupid and Psyche tale in books four through six of The Golden Ass.
claims.statement_id: Apuleius menceritakan kisah Cupid dan Psyche dalam buku empat sampai enam The Golden Ass.
claims.quote: Apuleius dedicates books four through six of The Golden Ass to this tale.

claims.statement: The tale appears in Greek art from the fourth century BCE.
claims.statement_id: Gambaran kisah Psyche dan Cupid sudah ada dalam seni Yunani abad keempat sebelum Masehi.
claims.quote: the story of Psyche and Eros (Cupid) can be found depicted in Greek art dating back to the 4th century BCE

claims.statement: In the Aeneid, Cupid disguises himself as Iulus.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Aeneid, Cupid menyamar sebagai Iulus.
claims.quote: In the Aeneid, the national epic of Rome by the poet Virgil, Cupid disguises himself as Iulus

claims.statement: In that form Cupid makes Queen Dido fall in love with the hero.
claims.statement_id: Penyamaran itu membuat Ratu Dido jatuh cinta pada sang pahlawan.
claims.quote: in this form he beguiles Queen Dido of Carthage to fall in love with the hero

claims.statement: In paintings Cupid can symbolize love without acting in the scene.
claims.statement_id: Dalam lukisan, Cupid dapat menandai pentingnya cinta tanpa menjadi pelaku utama.
claims.quote: He often does not play an active part when pictorially represented, but is included to signify the importance of love

claims.statement: Eos is the rosy-fingered goddess of dawn.
claims.statement_id: Eos ialah dewi fajar berjari kemerahan.
claims.quote: EOS was the rosy-fingered goddess of the dawn.

claims.statement: Eos personifies dawn in Greek mythology.
claims.statement_id: Eos personifikasi fajar dalam mitologi Yunani.
claims.quote: Eos is the personification and goddess of the dawn in Greek mythology.

claims.statement: Eos is daughter of Hyperion and Theia.
claims.statement_id: Eos anak Hyperion dan Theia.
claims.quote: She is the daughter of the Titans Hyperion and Theia

claims.statement: Helios and Selene are Eos's siblings.
claims.statement_id: Helios dan Selene adalah saudara Eos.
claims.quote: the sister of Helios (Sun) and Selene (Moon)

claims.statement: Eos rises from Okeanos at the start of each day.
claims.statement_id: Eos muncul dari sungai Okeanos setiap awal hari.
claims.quote: Eos rose into the sky from the river Okeanos (Oceanus) at the start of each day

claims.statement: Her light disperses the mists of night.
claims.statement_id: Cahayanya mengusir kabut malam.
claims.quote: with her rays of light dispersed the mists of night

claims.statement: Eos is depicted in a chariot drawn by winged horses or with her own wings.
claims.statement_id: Eos digambarkan berkendara dengan kuda bersayap atau terbang dengan sayapnya sendiri.
claims.quote: She was depicted either driving a chariot drawn by winged horses or borne aloft on her own wings.

claims.statement: Eos travels before Helios to announce the day.
claims.statement_id: Eos mendahului Helios dan menandai datangnya hari.
claims.quote: Eos rode in front of her brother Helios & announced the coming of the day.

claims.statement: Eos and Astraeus parented the wind gods.
claims.statement_id: Eos dan Astraeus menjadi orang tua para dewa angin.
claims.quote: Together they had the four Anemoi (wind gods)

claims.statement: Eos was mother of Memnon.
claims.statement_id: Eos adalah ibu Memnon.
claims.quote: Eos was also the mother of Memnon, the king of Ethiopia who fought in the Trojan War.

claims.statement: Eos asked Zeus to make Tithonus immortal.
claims.statement_id: Eos memohon Zeus memberi Tithonus keabadian.
claims.quote: She pleaded for Zeus to make Tithonus immortal, which Zeus assented to.

claims.statement: Eos forgot to ask for eternal youth for Tithonus.
claims.statement_id: Namun Eos lupa memohon masa muda abadi bagi Tithonus.
claims.quote: she forgot to ask Zeus to also grant him eternal youth.

claims.statement: In the Memnon tale, Eos's tears fell as dew.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Memnon, tangis Eos menjadi embun.
claims.quote: After he died, Eos wept, and her tears fell to the earth as dew.

claims.statement: Aurora is the Roman counterpart of Eos.
claims.statement_id: Aurora ialah padanan Romawi Eos.
claims.quote: the Roman goddess of the dawn, corresponding to the Greek goddess Eos.

claims.statement: No religious rite specifically for Eos is known.
claims.statement_id: Tidak diketahui ritus keagamaan khusus bagi Eos.
claims.quote: Unlike most of her relatives, Eos has no known religious rite.

claims.statement: Eos and Tithonus had Emathion and Memnon.
claims.statement_id: Eos dan Tithonus memiliki dua anak, Emathion dan Memnon.
claims.quote: Eos and Tithonus had two sons together, Emathion and Memnon.

claims.statement: HYDRA LERNAIA (Lernaean Hydra) was a gigantic, nine-headed water-serpent, which haunted the swamps of Lerna.
claims.statement_id: Lernaean Hydra terkait dengan HYDRA LERNAIA (Lernaean Hydra) was a gigantic, nine-headed water-serpent, which haunted the swamps of Lerna.
claims.quote: HYDRA LERNAIA (Lernaean Hydra) was a gigantic, nine-headed water-serpent, which haunted the swamps of Lerna.

claims.quote: As a second labor, Herakles was instructed to slay the Lernaean Hydra, a serpentlike creature with nine heads and poisonous venom

claims.statement_id: Lernaean Hydra terkait dengan That creature, bred in the swamp of Lerna, used to go forth into the plain and ravage both the cattle and the country.

claims.statement: Nor could he effect anything by smashing its heads with his club, for as fast as one head was smashed there grew up two.

claims.statement: Iolaus burned the roots of the heads so they would not sprout again.
claims.statement_id: Iolaus membakar pangkal kepala sehingga tidak tumbuh lagi.
claims.quote: called for help on Iolaus who, by setting fire to a piece of the neighboring wood and burning the roots of the heads with the brands, prevented them from sprouting.

claims.statement: he chopped off the immortal head, and buried it, and put a heavy rock on it
claims.statement_id: Lernaean Hydra terkait dengan he chopped off the immortal head, and buried it, and put a heavy rock on it
claims.quote: he chopped off the immortal head, and buried it, and put a heavy rock on it

claims.statement: But the body of the hydra he slit up and dipped his arrows in the gall.

claims.quote: But the body of the hydra he slit up and dipped his arrows in the gall.

claims.statement: Eurystheus said that this labour should not be reckoned among the ten because he had not got the better of the hydra by himself, but with the help of Iolaus.
claims.statement_id: Lernaean Hydra terkait dengan Eurystheus said that this labour should not be reckoned among the ten because he had not got the better of the hydra by himself, but with the help of Iolaus.

claims.statement: Helped by his faithful companion and nephew Iolaos, who used fire to stop the heads re-growing, Hercules eventually killed the Hydra and dipped his arrows in its poisonous blood.
